# Parameter Foundry (Jenkins plugin)

> Jenkins plugin that provides one parameter model for choices and typed input
> across the UI, Pipeline, REST, CLI, Rebuild, and downstream builds. Values are
> canonical, providers are governed, and the core never executes Job-supplied
> code.

Repository: https://github.com/xykong/parameter-foundry-plugin
Plugin short name: `parameter-foundry`
Current symbols: `foundryChoice`, `foundryForm`, `foundryFile`, `foundryBase64File`, `foundryStashedFile`, `withFoundryFileParameter`, `foundryParameterText`

## Start here

- [User guide index](docs/guide/README.md): who the guide is for and where to go next
- [Getting started](docs/guide/getting-started.md): five-minute walkthrough
- [Parameter reference](docs/guide/parameters.md): every field, default, and transport
- [Saved parameter text](docs/guide/pipeline-parameter-text.md): current-build legacy raw strings, explicit missing-value fallbacks, security filtering and unsupported historical values
- [File parameters](docs/guide/file-parameters.md): bounded workspace/Base64/stash upload, Pipeline wrappers and migration
- [Cookbook](docs/guide/examples.md): copy-pasteable configurations
- [Providers](docs/guide/providers.md): static, managed config, REST, script, Git refs
- [Whole-response REST choices](docs/guide/raw-rest-responses.md): exact UTF-8 literals, trailing choices, explicit DNS/TLS failure declarations and uncached recovery; `rawStatusPolicy` defaults to `http-status`; opt-in `native-nonredirect-body` reads only 304/306/308 and 302 without Location as bodies, does not enable redirects; separate `rawRedirectTargets` plus Profile opt-in permit finite same-origin destinations under one budget, with `matchUri` failure selectors and an explicit `REDIRECT_LIMIT` mapping; `foundryRawLiteral` and `foundryRawFailureChoice` configure raw response data; TLS keys are finite admin declarations, never a verification bypass or automatic failure-reason classification
- Git `sortOrder: none` preserves unsorted List Git Branches category order through Java HashSet iteration; full-ref values and combined-category grouping require separate verification.
- Uncached Git ref Providers (`cacheTtlSeconds: 0`) do not reuse the generic five-second failure cooldown. Each subsequent lookup retries through existing request budgets and in-flight sharing; explicit fallback policy remains unchanged. Error-text option equivalence is a separate migration gate.
- Git `gitSelectionMode: none` leaves multi-row list renderers and explicitly sized searchable lists unselected. In `default` mode these lists also remain unselected when no exact/containing default match exists, including after filtering; dropdown and unconfigured searchable first-option behavior is unchanged. API defaults remain independent.
- [Migration](docs/guide/migration.md): moving off Active Choices, Extended Choice, List Git Branches, and others
- [Best practices](docs/guide/best-practices.md): modelling, defaults, security, scale
- [Design goals](docs/guide/design-goals.md): principles, scope, non-goals
- [Troubleshooting](docs/guide/troubleshooting.md): stable error codes and common situations
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): released changes per version

## Core concepts

- `foundryChoice` with `selectionMode: single` returns a string or `null`.
- `foundryChoice` with `selectionMode: multiple` returns an unordered list sorted by machine value.
- `renderer: table` makes the matrix cells the selectable values; missing cells are unavailable and
  disabled cells stay unselectable.
- `foundryForm` returns a typed map or JSON object built from its field schema.
- Options come from inline `choices` or from a Provider referenced by `providerId`; `dependsOn`
  makes the parameter reactive.
- Providers resolve through Connection Profiles that declare base URL, credentials, path and query
  allow-lists, timeouts, and response size bounds.
- Provider types: `foundryStaticProvider`, `foundryManagedConfigProvider`, `foundryRestProvider`,
  `foundryGitRefProvider`, `foundryScriptProvider` (reviewed companion engine), and
  `foundryMappingProvider` for a dependency value → option list mapping with a default list; the
  mapping executes nothing.
- Environment export: `string` or `none` for single selection, `delimited`, `json`, or `none` for
  multiple selection, `json` or `none` plus per-field variables for forms.
- Static multiple choices can use `standardApiInputMode: extended-choice` for source-compatible
  repeated REST fields, comma-split CLI and delimited form JSON. Pair it with submitted export
  order and duplicate deduplication; repeated supported values remain in the exported string.
  Extended Choice list/checkbox browser forms submit in declared option order; explicit API
  inputs retain their caller order, and canonical values remain sorted.
  The next snapshot permits empty static multiple-choice option lists in this mode:
  omitted CLI input preserves the literal default. Set legacyEmptyOptionsOmitCli for
  missing/blank source options so explicit input returns no parameter; comma-only configured
  options leave this flag off and explicit input returns an existing empty-string parameter.
  Comma-only CLI input follows the omitted-input default path.
  Identical duplicate Inline options are supported for legacy list/checkbox multiple selection
  with selectedDisplay none, duplicatePolicy deduplicate and custom values disabled.
  Each displayed entry has independent selection; repeated submitted values retain declared order.
  Ordinary modes and conflicting duplicate metadata still reject duplicate options.
  Version 0.7.288 has known gaps for literal/blank defaults, unlisted form values,
  single selection and custom delimiters. Do not infer full parity from adapter
  classification; see [source contract](docs/research/extended-choice-static-transport-contract.md).
  Version 0.8.296 adds `legacyDefaultLiteral` for exact
  omitted-input environment defaults and distinguishes no ParameterValue from an
  explicit empty selection. Canonical values remain lists; explicit typed arrays
  stay strict. Form strings remain literal and arrays join without filtering the
  exported string; Rebuild keeps an editable historical literal. Compatibility
  requires submitted order and delimited/disabled export. Static single compatibility is implemented and passes characterized source/browser gates.
  Single CLI/standard fields filter and join into a scalar; form literals remain raw,
  and API defaults are independent of UI defaults. Explicit typed strings stay strict.
  `legacyEmptyChoiceAllowed` preserves source empty CLI/standard token separators;
  no empty option is added to the UI/canonical list. Ordinary and typed input stay
  strict. Candidate verification passes 365 tests, 9,792 source factory cases and
  22 browser checks; exact release and per-Job source/consumer/history gates remain.
- Unreleased Git history fix: `standardApiInputMode: list-git-branches` copies readable historical StringParameterValue subclasses into transient editable Rebuild defaults, preserving literal text and current Job defaults. Empty form submission retains the source fallback; sensitive values are excluded. This adds no source-class deserializer or uninstall approval.
- Provider-backed single choices without dependencies can use `standardApiInputMode: list-git-branches`: literal unlisted revisions remain accepted, explicit inputs/defaults do not fetch Git, and supplied snapshots retain binding/expiry validation. `gitSelectionMode` preserves dropdown selection independently of API/CLI defaults.
- Typed API: `…/parameter-foundry/api/v1/{schema,resolve,validate,build,providers/health,import/preview}`.
- Errors carry stable codes such as `PARAMETER_FOUNDRY_UNKNOWN_VALUE`.
- Migration CLI: `parameter-foundry-migration` scans the controller, previews a
  Job with its decisions and exact diff, and applies one atomic batch per Job;
  `parameter-foundry-migration-verify` stores the before/after A/B evidence on
  the migration record.
- A parameter that the Job's Pipeline declares is reported as blocked: the
  Jenkinsfile has to change, because Declarative re-applies the declared
  parameters at every build and would revert a configuration migration.
- Read-only replacement simulation: `…/parameter-foundry-replacement-simulation/report`
  compares every production Job's recorded values and environment exports with
  the simulated foundry control and reports `EQUIVALENT`, `MISMATCH`,
  `NEEDS_PROVIDER`, `MANUAL_REDESIGN`, `UNVERIFIED`, or `BLOCKED` per parameter.
- The migration page, the retirement dashboard, and every adapter reason,
  decision, fact, and verification case ship in English, Chinese, Japanese, and
  Korean.

## Conventions for generated content

- Prefer Provider-backed parameters over copied option lists.
- Keep machine values stable; change labels, not values.
- Use `defaultMode: none` unless a default is genuinely safe.
- Validate via `api/v1/validate` before scheduling when building tooling.

## Boundaries

- The core plugin never executes Job-supplied Groovy, JavaScript, HTML, or reads controller file
  paths. Scripting and custom rendering live behind reviewed companion contracts.
- Foundry file parameters ship in the single HPI without File Parameters dependencies.
  Rejected HTTP/CLI uploads and cancelled queue items release pending data immediately;
  crash recovery protects active uploads and admitted queue/build ownership.
  `foundryFile` selects workspace, base64 or stash delivery.
  maxUploadBytes=0 inherits 1 MiB decoded bytes for Base64 or 100 MiB for workspace/stash;
  positive limits override defaults and are enforced for UI/API/CLI, downstream delivery and Rebuild.
  Workspace mode automatically places files in Freestyle and uses withFoundryFileParameter in Pipeline;
  it preserves Core relative destinations and original filename environment keys.
  UI/REST multipart and CLI share bounded ingestion. Typed JSON rejects binary definitions.
  Source file migrations are class B; wrappers change to withFoundryFileParameter,
  ordinary unstash keeps its name, and binary lifecycle needs manual verification.
  Keep source plugins until historical and generated references are retired.

## Internal references (for contributors and reviewers)

- [Requirements manifest](docs/testing/requirements.yaml)
- [Acceptance cases and known issues](docs/testing/acceptance-cases.md)
- [Product specification](docs/product/product-spec.md)
- [Core architecture](docs/architecture/core-architecture.md)
- [Architecture decisions](docs/decisions/)
- [Production verification records](docs/testing/)

- Version 0.9.299: single `standardApiInputMode: active-choices` preserves
  unflagged source string transports and Core StringParameterValue history/queue/env aliases.
  `activeChoicesApiDefaultMode: first|literal` and `activeChoicesApiDefaultLiteral`
  separate omitted API defaults from radio/dropdown UI defaults. Ordinary/typed explicit
  values stay strict; supplied snapshots remain validated. No source scripts execute.
  Node Provider `source: configured-nodes` preserves built-in-first configured order,
  including offline/zero-executor nodes. Existing nodes/labels modes retain behavior.
  Exact 0.9.299 release gates pass; per-Job migration gates remain; see UP-AC-043.

- Version 0.9.301 fixes configured-node empty-name filtering to match
  Java `String.trim()` source semantics; it preserves Unicode whitespace and
  original leading/trailing spaces. UP-AC-044 shared-resolution and exact release browser gates pass; full regression passes 375 tests. Per-Job migration and retirement gates remain.

- Literal Active Choices preview targets use the single compatibility mode only
  for unflagged, unfiltered choices without dependencies or cached
  defaults. Preserve descriptions, first API defaults and dropdown/radio UI
  defaults. Snapshot UP-AC-045 passes 378 regression tests, 44/44 adapter factory cases,
  real-browser defaults and description snippet round-trip. It is not deployed;
  per-Job, exact release and retirement gates remain.

- Version 0.10.304 single active-choices mode supports one empty inline option,
  preserving its position, empty-string submission and typed empty vs null.
  UP-AC-046 passes 380 Harness tests, 132/132 source cases, six browser pairs,
  twelve empty-string form builds and editable Core history. The exact release artifact passes the same gates; per-Job acceptance remains.

- Reactive single `active-choices` compatibility requires a Provider and `activeChoicesApiDefaultMode: literal`;
  omitted input uses the configured fallback string, explicit legacy strings do not resolve options,
  and optional snapshots bind dependencies. Typed explicit input stays strict. This transport feature
  does not establish generic REST response or real-browser source parity.

- REST `responseMode` defaults to `mapped`; `active-choices-choice` and
  `active-choices-cascade` interpret reviewed JSON data-or-root single dropdown
  responses without executing Groovy. They preserve source metadata and separate
  ordinary API defaults (including marked comma joins/raw first keys) from UI
  selection. Cascades retain independent literal API defaults. Mapping paths and
  transforms do not apply. Configure a governed Connection Profile, source
  fallback options and live caching policy; per-Job/browser/form and retirement
  verification remain required. See the Providers guide.

- Reviewed single REST source filters preserve per-parameter activeChoicesFilterLength (default 1); copy source filterLength when migrating. Short nonempty filters retain the previous list; clearing rebuilds it.

- Reviewed Active Choices single Mapping Providers reset UI selection on dependency changes; renderer select has no source regex filter. Literal API defaults are independent; option resolution requires declared dependencies. Ordinary mapping Providers retain valid selections.

Choice list renderers accept `visibleItemCount` (0 for automatic sizing, 1–1000 for an explicit row count). It affects display height only, applies with and without JavaScript, and does not limit options or selections. Extended Choice multiple-list migration preserves positive configured row counts. Legacy zero-row sizing needs separate UI verification.

- Unreleased Active Choices multiple transport uses `standardApiInputMode: active-choices`, `selectionMode: multiple`, and `environmentExport: string`. Standard callers preserve Core strings; typed explicit arrays retain membership validation. UI empty selection and API first/literal defaults are independent. Non-empty option values are required; filtering, refresh and formatted HTML need separate source/browser verification.

- Reviewed Active Choices UI policies: `activeChoicesFilterMode` auto/none/regex and `activeChoicesRefreshMode` default/retain-valid. Defaults retain existing behavior. Regex uses source lowercase/minimum-length rules; successful multiple filtering clears selection. Policy changes invalidate snapshots and must survive configuration/snippet/Rebuild copies. HTML reference migration remains separate.

Literal presentation references use `foundryReference`; see [parameter types](docs/guide/parameters.md).

- Source-specific history readers introduced in 0.21.349: `legacyGitHistoryEnabled` and `legacyExtendedChoiceHistoryEnabled` independently default false and take effect only after full restart. Each requires source absence, its own immutable resource integrity and class ownership. Initial Core targets 2.528.3/2.568.3; Beta/internal API exception is method-local and checker remains enabled. Status conflicts invalidate acceptance; hot native reinstall unsupported. Extended Choice covers historical strings after current native definitions/generators are migrated; preserve JSON-file consumers separately. Source definitions/Replay and file history are independent gates. See [history guide](docs/guide/history-compatibility.md). Isolated product tests do not approve production activation or source removal.

- Unreleased File history development: `legacyFileHistoryEnabled` defaults false,
  `legacyFileHistoryMaxBytes` defaults 100 MiB; both require full restart. A fixed
  isolated bundle supplies completed Base64/local stash shapes and passive graph
  metadata only. Four class owners and descriptor/Symbol discovery precede ACTIVE;
  every binary open checks live acceptance. Job.READ plus Core-filtered Run value
  identity precedes download. No upload definitions, native Delete, pending tmpFile
  reader or remote fallback. Active wrappers, pending uploads, Rebuild/Replay,
  producer migration and exact-HPI both-Core/HTTP/browser validation remain gates.
  Keep native source installed until full workflow fidelity is proved. See
  [history guide](docs/guide/history-compatibility.md).

Static Extended Choice multiple migrations may set `valueTransport: 'core-string'` to save an actual Jenkins `StringParameterValue`. Pipeline `params`, build API values and environment exports retain the source-compatible string. Form strings preserve order, spaces and empty tokens; CLI and repeated fields retain the original trimming and unavailable-value filtering rules. This avoids rewriting scripts that consume the old string directly. The default `typed` transport keeps multiple values as a list. Core string transport requires static `extended-choice` multiple compatibility with `delimited` environment export; Provider-backed choices keep typed transport.

- [Public-source preparation and history isolation](docs/security/open-source-preparation.md)

Historical Rebuild scalar strings for multiple choices in delimited mode are split with the configured literal delimiter and validated individually; native arrays are never split. See UP-AC-079 in docs/testing/acceptance-cases.md.
